commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

content.text:
The New Project form now has a "Template" choice with two templates, and both come from a new `project-templates/` folder that's built into the app. All tests pass (170, 1 ignored), and a project created from either template builds with `piton build`.

**The templates:**
- **Base:** just an empty `index.pi` in the spec root, the same as New Project did before.
- **Scope, concept, and shape:**
  - `lib/Scope.pi`, `lib/Concept.pi` and `lib/Shape.pi`, the same abstract anchors this repo's own spec uses;
  - `lib/index.pi`, exporting them;
  - an `index.pi` that uses the lib;
  - an example `ApplicationScope` with its concept and shape in `scope/application/index.pi`.

**How the folder works:** each template is a folder holding `template.json` (name, description and order) and a `spec/` folder. The files in `spec/` are copied into the new project's spec root. At build time, `build.rs` bakes every file in with `include_str!`, so editing or adding a template changes what the next build offers. A template with no `spec/` folder gets an empty `index.pi`, like Base. Files already in the spec root are never overwritten.

**In the form:** the Template group sits after the Git checkbox. It's one radio button per template, with its description underneath, and the first (Base) selected to start with.

**Code:**
- `src/project_templates.rs`: reads the built-in templates and writes their files.
- `build.rs`: embeds them.
- `src/new_project.rs`: adds the template choice to the form and to project creation.

**Tests:**
- **Built-in templates:** a new test checks both templates are there, in order, with their files.
- **Project creation:**
  - builds a project from the scope-concept-shape template and runs `piton build` on it;
  - checks an existing `index.pi` isn't overwritten.
- **Form:** picks the second template and checks its lib files are written.

**Spec:** `spec/scope/new-project/index.pi` has a new `templates` section describing the two templates and the `project-templates/` folder, and its `creating` section now says the chosen template's files are written. `piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` all ran cleanly, and the app builds with no warnings.

`project-templates/` is new and untracked, so add it when you commit.
